big_case_rationale: Major doctrinal decision resolving a deep circuit split on whether Stinson v. United States (1993) survives Kisor v. Wilkie (2019) and Loper Bright (2024) for U.S. Sentencing Guidelines commentary, affecting how federal courts calculate advisory ranges in ~66,000 sentencings annually.

semantic_claims.proposition: The Court holds that Stinson v. United States, 508 U.S. 36 (1993), continues to govern judicial deference to Sentencing Guidelines commentary without modification by Kisor v. Wilkie, 588 U.S. 558 (2019), or Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. 369 (2024), because the Sentencing Reform Act (28 U.S.C. 994(a)(1)-(2), 18 U.S.C. 3553(a)-(b)), Williams v. United States, 503 U.S. 193 (1992), and U.S.S.G. 1B1.7 establish an integrated system of non-binding post-Booker sentencing advice in which commentary is authoritative in calculating the Commission's recommended advisory range unless it violates the Constitution or a federal statute or is inconsistent with, or a plainly erroneous reading of, the guideline text.

The Court states a categorical rule applicable to all official commentary in the Sentencing Guidelines Manual across federal sentencings generally, rather than confining its holding to U.S.S.G. 2K2.1(a)(3)'s large-capacity-magazine enhancement or resolving the case on case-specific harmless-error grounds.
